title: Genesis AI raises $500 million to deploy glove-wearing robots
slides: Can Genesis AI's gloves outwork human hands?
It raised $500 million to deploy them
Investors bet on dexterity over intelligence
Factories may soon test these robots first
Ask which tasks your team could hand off
thread_text:
1. The $500M bet on hands

Genesis AI just raised half a billion dollars to build robotic gloves that match human dexterity. The money isn't going to smarter AI—it's going to better hands.

2. Why dexterity wins now

Investors are shifting focus from artificial intelligence to physical manipulation. A robot that can't grip a tool is useless, no matter how smart its brain.

3. Factories first, homes later

Manufacturing floors will be the first testing ground for these gloves. If they can handle assembly lines, the rest of the labor market is next.

4. The tasks you could hand off

Start by listing repetitive manual tasks your team does daily. Those are the first candidates for robotic hands, not entire jobs.

5. Audit your own workflow

Look at your calendar today: which physical or repetitive task could a robot do? If you can name one, you’re already behind.
